verdict.rationale: LibreChat's docs say agents can gain file system access through MCP servers, which can be added at runtime. Its built-in code execution is described as secure, zero-setup execution, which reads as a sandboxed interpreter rather than a shell on the user's own machine. Missing for 10: documented native command/shell execution on the host machine, first-party file-editing tools, details of how MCP file access edits local files, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, the assistant can run commands and edit files on my machine — a real exec surface, not just chat about what to do

citations.quote: LibreChat leverages MCP to dramatically expand what your AI agents can do, allowing you to integrate everything from file system access, web browsers, specialized APIs, to custom business tools.
Execute code in multiple languages securely with zero setup
Adding and updating servers at runtime from the MCP Settings panel, without editing a config file or restarting
